findings.location: Methods, Diagnostic prediction model vs bp_work/data/GC-diagnosis-model/Xtest.xlsx (142 rows)
findings.evidence: The paper reports 'n test set 1' = 152 participants (Methods, Diagnostic prediction model); the authors' own stored output (bp_work/data/GC-diagnosis-model/Xtest.xlsx (142 rows)) gives 142. Our re-run gives 142, which matches the stored output.
'external test sensitivity' is reported with different values. Abstract: 0.95 proportion | Results p.3: 0.905 proportion. Agreeing reports: 1 location(s) [Abstract] vs 1 [Results p.3].

The paper reports 'specificity test set 1' = 0.926 proportion (Results p.3); the authors' own stored output (bp_work/results/GC-diagnosis-model/GC-diagnosis-model-pred-score-for-test.xlsx) gives 0.936. Our re-run gives 0.9362, which matches the stored output. The gap is small (<5%): it may be run-to-run variation if the stored output came from a different run.

The Abstract gives 0.950 ('...ite GC diagnostic model, which is validated in an external test set with a sensitivity of 0.950, outperforming conventional methods lev...'); the body never states 0.950. The body sentence about the same quantity (shared words: sensitivity, validated) gives 0.944: '...Next, we trained a random forest model with the 10 essential features, and then validated the model in the test set 1, yielding an area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) of 0.967 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.944-0.987,...'. Confirm that both refer to the same quantity (same cohort, test set, metric) before keeping it.

The paper reports "95% confidence" intervals, but the code computes the interval with 5%/95% bounds (`confidence_lower = sorted_scores[int(0.05 * len(sorted_scores))]`) (and 1 similar line(s)), which is a 90% interval; no 2.5%/97.5% bounds appear anywhere in the code. Check whether the reported intervals are 90% intervals.

The text reports an additional study or analysis: 'The 10-DM model was further validated in a prospective cohort of 214 participants recruited at a fourth centre, with an AUROC of 0.941 (sensitivity: 0.912, specificity: 0.833).'. Its head count 214 appears nowhere else in the paper, the phrase 'fourth centre' is used in no other sentence (the Methods do not describe it), the sentence cites no source, and the code, README and file names in the materials do not contain the number. Look for its data, code, table or supplementary item; if there is none, the analysis cannot be checked from what was released.
